newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 22.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday extended sympathy to the government and the people of Bangladesh for the loss of lives and property in Monday's cyclone.
The United States offered help Tuesday to Bangladesh cyclone victims.
A joint team of Indian Tripura state officials and tribal refugee leaders will visit Khagrachari hill district from May 29 to see rehabilitation of the repatriated refugees.

The Developing-8 Group comprising eight Islamic countries has identified 30 areas of cooperation in its draft declaration which will be adopted at the first summit level meeting scheduled to be held on June 14 and 15 in Turkey.
The national budget for the financial year 1997-98 is likely to be placed before the parliament on June 12.
Some 268,154 families were affected by Monday's cyclone, according to Bangladesh Red Crescent Society.
A marginal shortfall is anticipated in the revenue collection in the current fiscal fiscal (1996-97).
Short supply of sugarcane over the past two years has led drastic reduction in output at the sugar mills. REUTER
